name: Valant vs Freed
title: Valant vs Freed: Psychiatry EHR vs AI Scribe Comparison
description: Compare Valant (psychiatry-focused EHR) and Freed (AI scribe). Understand how these complementary tools serve different purposes for psychiatric practices.

summary.bottom_line: Valant and Freed are complementary tools for psychiatry practices. Valant is a psychiatrist-designed EHR with e-prescribing (including controlled substances), measurement-based care, and practice management. Freed is an AI scribe that generates psychiatric notes from patient visits. Valant runs your practice; Freed speeds up documentation. Psychiatrists might use both together.

sections.heading: Valant vs Freed: Overview
sections.content: Valant and Freed address different needs for psychiatric practices. Valant is a psychiatrist-designed EHR offering e-prescribing with EPCS certification for controlled substances, measurement-based care with integrated outcome tracking (PHQ-9, GAD-7), scheduling, billing, patient portal, and telehealth. Freed is an AI scribe that listens to psychiatric appointments and generates clinical notes. They serve different functions: Valant manages the practice, Freed accelerates documentation.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Valant uses quote-based pricing typical of psychiatry-focused EHRs (often $200-400+/month per provider for full features). Freed costs $39-119/month. Using both would increase total cost but may be worthwhile if documentation is a significant time burden. Valant's value is in its psychiatry-specific features (EPCS, measurement-based care); Freed's value is in time savings on notes.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Valant provides: EPCS-certified e-prescribing for controlled substances (critical for psychiatry), integrated PHQ-9/GAD-7 outcome tracking, patient self-scheduling, billing and revenue cycle management, MYIO patient portal, and psychiatry-specific workflows. Freed provides: ambient listening during sessions, AI-generated psychiatry notes, therapy progress notes, ICD-10 suggestions (Premier), and mobile app. Valant handles practice operations; Freed handles note generation.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: These tools serve different purposes for psychiatrists:

recommendations.when: You need a psychiatry-specific EHR with EPCS e-prescribing and measurement-based care, and are comfortable writing notes using Valant's psychiatric templates
You want Valant's psychiatric practice management features AND want to reduce documentation time—Freed supports psychiatry note formats
Never for psychiatrists—you need an EHR like Valant for e-prescribing controlled substances, which is essential for psychiatric practice

faqs.a: Freed does not list Valant as a native push integration. You would use Freed to generate notes during sessions, then copy the content into Valant. Freed supports psychiatry note formats which align with psychiatric documentation needs.

faqs.q: Can Freed replace Valant for psychiatrists?
faqs.a: No. Freed cannot prescribe medications, track outcome measures, process insurance claims, or manage scheduling. Psychiatrists need an EHR with e-prescribing (especially EPCS for controlled substances). Freed only generates notes.

Valant does not have ambient AI listening like Freed. Valant provides psychiatry-specific documentation templates, but note generation is manual. For AI-assisted documentation, you would add Freed or a similar tool.

faqs.q: Which is more important for psychiatrists?
faqs.a: Valant (or another psychiatry EHR) is essential—you need e-prescribing for medications. Freed is optional but helpful if documentation is time-consuming. Most psychiatrists need an EHR first, then may add an AI scribe.
